question: Can a tight, method-independent PaiNN-native index-one saddle set be built for the paired GAD/Sella benchmark?
hypothesis: The coarse native-set smoke establishes that T1x endpoint pairs can yield PaiNN-native index-one maxima; tighter endpoint and NEB tolerances will retain a usable subset.
decision_rule: Accept only if both PaiNN endpoint relaxations converge at fmax <= 0.005 eV/A, climbing NEB converges at fmax <= 0.01 eV/A, the maximum image has fmax <= 0.01 eV/A, and the full mass-weighted Eckart-projected Hessian has n_neg = 1. Then require two-sided native endpoint validation before optimization tests.

resources.allocation: one A100 3g.20gb MIG slice, 4 CPU cores, 20G memory, 90 minutes

result: Three of the first three endpoint pairs produced accepted candidates: both endpoint relaxations converged below 0.005 eV/A; climbing NEB converged; maximum-image fmax values were 0.00951, 0.00122, and 0.0000207 eV/A; all had projected n_neg=1. This is not connectivity validation.
next_action: Validate all three candidates in both downhill directions against their PaiNN-relaxed endpoint minima, then run the frozen paired GAD/Sella pilot only on validated candidates.
